one_liner: Arduino TFT driver plus drawing library for ESP32, RP2040, ESP8266 and STM32; 1.3x to 4.7x faster than Adafruit_GFX on an ILI9341 at 40 MHz.
what_it_does: TFT_eSPI drives small SPI and 8/16-bit parallel TFT panels (ILI9341, ST7789, ST7735, ST7796, ILI9488, GC9A01 and about 20 other controllers) and draws primitives, bitmap and anti-aliased fonts, images and off-screen Sprites (1, 4, 8 or 16-bit colour) on them. The API keeps Adafruit_GFX names (drawPixel, drawLine, fillRect, drawCircle, setTextColor, print), so most Adafruit sketches port by swapping the constructor and colour constants, as the benchmark sketches show. Unlike Adafruit_GFX, the panel, pins, SPI clock and fonts are chosen at compile time in User_Setup.h or User_Setup_Select.h inside the library folder (or PlatformIO build flags), not in the sketch.
how_it_is_fast: On ESP32 it bypasses the Arduino SPI library and writes the SPI peripheral registers directly (TFT_WRITE_BITS sets the length register, the W0 data register and the SPI_USR start bit), and toggles DC and CS with single GPIO set/clear register writes. Solid fills (pushBlock) load the 64-byte W0-W15 buffer with the colour once and re-trigger 512-bit transfers, so a fill streams at the SPI link rate; fillScreen reached 98% of the 40 MHz link limit in the benchmark versus 78% for Adafruit_GFX (derived from page data). drawPixel caches the last column and row address and skips re-sending CASET or PASET when they are unchanged. drawLine splits Bresenham's line into horizontal or vertical runs drawn with drawFastHLine/drawFastVLine, circles are drawn as runs too, and one bus transaction is held across a whole primitive (inTransaction) instead of one per pixel.
when_to_use: Arduino or PlatformIO firmware on ESP32, ESP32-S2/S3/C3, RP2040, ESP8266 or STM32F/L4 driving a supported SPI panel, where Adafruit_GFX plus a controller driver is too slow for pixel-, line- and text-heavy screens.
Per-pixel or line-heavy drawing (plots, gauges, wireframes): it had the fastest Pixels (775,781 us) and Lines (264,950 us) rows of the four libraries measured.
RP2040 with 8- or 16-bit parallel panels driven by PIO, with DMA, which the README reports at 4 ms to clear a 320x480 screen.

Projects that want a large example set and ecosystem: Sprites for flicker-free updates, vlw smooth fonts from flash arrays or LittleFS, OpenFontRender TrueType add-on, TFT_eWidget GUI widgets, XPT2046 touch.
Porting an existing Adafruit_GFX sketch with minimal source changes.
when_not_to_use: Recent ESP32 Arduino cores and new chips: open issues report ESP32-S3 boot crashes on cores newer than 2.0.14 (#3329) and that ESP32-C6/H2 on core 3.0.x need local modifications (#3438). The Feb 2026 commits fix DMA on C3/S3 for 3.x board packages, but the last tagged release, V2.5.43 (6 March), predates them.

When raw speed on ESP32 SPI is the only criterion: LovyanGFX beat it on 9 of the 13 rows both ran in the same 2021 run (TFT_eSPI won only Text, Pixels, Lines and outline Circles), by up to 17% (Rounded rects outline 13,089 vs 15,371 us), and also ran the Arcs rows that TFT_eSPI lacked then (derived from page data).

Fill-dominated screens: fills are bound by the SPI clock, so at 40 MHz the gain over Adafruit_GFX is only 1.25x to 1.3x (Screen fill 1.26x, Rectangles filled 1.26x, Rounded rects filled 1.26x); a faster bus, a parallel panel or partial redraws matter more.
Generic Arduino boards outside the optimised list: the README says they fall back to the slower Arduino SPI calls, and only SPI panels are supported there.
Projects needing runtime display selection or several different panels in one build: the configuration is compile-time and global to the library folder.
Desktop or vector-graphics work: it is an embedded panel driver with integer primitives, not a general path rasterizer like the Blend2D, Skia or AGG entries in this category.

integration.form: Arduino library compiled from source (TFT_eSPI.cpp plus a per-processor file); also usable as an ESP-IDF component that requires the arduino component
integration.dependencies: Arduino core for the target (SPI; FS/SPIFFS or LittleFS for smooth fonts loaded from flash); ESP-IDF spi_master driver for ESP32 DMA; Earle Philhower's arduino-pico core for RP2040 PIO features
integration.min_toolchain: Arduino IDE or PlatformIO; ESP32 Arduino board package 2.x.x or later for the ESP32 family (README); arduino-pico core for RP2040 PIO
integration.platforms: Optimised: RP2040, ESP32, ESP32-S2/S3/C3, ESP8266, STM32F1/F2/F4/F7 (DMA on ESP32, RP2040 and STM32 SPI); other 32-bit Arduino boards through generic Arduino SPI calls
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. The transaction flags (locked, inTransaction, lockTransaction) are plain bools with no RTOS mutex; on ESP32 SUPPORT_TRANSACTIONS is forced so SPI.beginTransaction takes the SPI HAL lock, but object state is unprotected, so drive one TFT_eSPI object from one task.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: drawing calls keep Adafruit_GFX names and signatures, but the constructor takes no pins (they come from User_Setup.h), colour constants are TFT_* rather than ILI9341_*, and init() replaces begin(freq)

gotchas: Configuration lives inside the library folder (User_Setup.h / User_Setup_Select.h); updating the library overwrites it unless you keep setups in a sibling folder as the README's Tips describe. The shipped default User_Setup.h sets SPI_FREQUENCY to 27 MHz, not the 40 MHz used in the benchmark.

On ESP32, pushBlock and drawPixel return before the last SPI transfer finishes (the 'Do not wait here' comment and tft_Write_16N); end_tft_write waits, but code that toggles the shared bus inside startWrite()/endWrite() must account for it. Sharing the bus with an SD card requires TFT_MISO/MOSI/SCLK to be defined explicitly (README).
DMA is used only by pushImageDMA/pushPixelsDMA; fillRect, lines and text always use the blocking register path, and DMA is unavailable for ILI9481/ILI9486/ILI9488 over SPI.

Smooth (vlw) fonts cannot be scaled with setTextSize, and a later change added the smooth-font background-rendering flag as a new setTextColor parameter, which the README calls breaking for some sketches.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick TFT_eSPI over LovyanGFX when per-pixel and line drawing dominate, you are on RP2040 parallel/PIO panels, or you rely on its Sprite, smooth-font and widget ecosystem; pick LovyanGFX for the fastest fills, shapes and arcs on ESP32 SPI, runtime panel configuration and better tracking of new ESP32 cores. Pick Arduino_GFX when you need its wider range of data-bus classes and panels; it was slower than both on lines, shapes and pixels but fastest on text in the same run.
verified_claims_summary: One single-pass run of moononournation's Arduino_graphicstest_PDQ (2021-06-16; Arduino IDE 1.8.15, arduino-esp32 1.0.6, TTGO T8 v1.8 ESP32, PSRAM off, ILI9341 over SPI at 40 MHz, no DMA; compiler flags, CPU clock and TFT_eSPI version not recorded) timed the same test body in each library: TFT_eSPI beat Adafruit_GFX with Adafruit_ILI9341 by 4.7x on outline circles, 4.5x on text, 4.0x on lines, 1.8x on pixels and 1.26-1.3x on fills. Timings stop after end_tft_write's SPI-busy wait, so they include the final transfer; the 2020 run of the same suite gave noticeably different TFT_eSPI numbers, and the README's own '3 to 10 times faster' claim has no benchmark behind it.
status_note: Active but slow-moving: after a gap from July 2024 to February 2026, a burst of commits (DMA fix for ESP32 C3/S3 on 3.x board packages, STM32L4 DMA, new setups) ends with a README update on 2026-04-03; master reports version 2.5.44 while the latest tagged release is V2.5.43, with 278 open issues and 75 open pull requests. The licence (FreeBSD two-clause for Bodmer's code plus Adafruit BSD and MIT notices) makes it copyable, and a June 2025 issue (#3770) calling it abandoned recommended LovyanGFX.
